title: Secondary-region throttle churn analysis & mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed a multi-region request amplification event during a sustained traffic spike that caused sustained SLO misses for hosted inference customers in EU-West. The incident involved (1) throttle churn in the secondary region due to aggressive circuit-breaker hysteresis settings, (2) ineffective cluster-level load-shedding rules that allowed internal queues to grow, and (3) KV-cache warmup delays after failover that amplified tail latency. Impact: several high-traffic customers experienced 99th-percentile generation latency above the SLO (target 150ms, observed 99p = 820ms) and an error rate spike from baseline 0.12% to 1.6% for a 38-minute window. The platform fallback behavior routed more requests to secondary variants, which in turn triggered further throttling and backpressure across GPUs. This ticket captures the incident analysis, proposed corrective actions, and the playbook for preventing recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18T10:12Z - First alerts: per-route latency > SLO (console dashboards). Automated alerting triggered on 99p latency threshold.
2026-02-18T10:15Z - On-call rotated to regional SRE. Initial mitigation: increased circuit-breaker thresholds in primary region to accept more inflight requests (temporary).
2026-02-18T10:22Z - Failover: Traffic steering policy routed ~30% of traffic to secondary region (eu-west-2) due to perceived primary saturation.
2026-02-18T10:28Z - Observed throttle churn: secondary region frontends repeatedly opening/closing CB, leading to request bursts and KV-cache cold starts.
2026-02-18T10:40Z - Implemented emergency load-shedding rule to drop non-authenticated polling requests and deprioritize large-batched background jobs. Latency began to improve.
2026-02-18T10:50Z - Rolling restart of a subset of worker pools in secondary region to clear stuck queues and rebalance GRPC channels.
2026-02-18T11:00Z - Incident declared mitigated by SRE; extra monitoring kept for 24h.
2026-02-19T09:00Z - Post-incident analysis kickoff. Gathered heap/queue samples, kernel traces, and circuit-breaker metrics.
root_causes: Circuit-breaker hysteresis tuned for aggressive fail-close behavior: thresholds and recovery windows were too narrow for the observed traffic shape, causing rapid open/close cycles (churn).
Load-shedding ruleset lacked priority classification for internal, non-customer traffic; internal background traffic amplified queueing during failover.

KV cache warmup and model shard balancing in secondary region had insufficient pre-warm policy during automated failover; cold KV cache and resharding added 200-400ms per-request overhead on the tail.
Smart routing policy mis-evaluated primary node health signals (using transient CPU load instead of sustained latency), prompting premature failover.
impact_summary: High: Multiple paying customers experienced SLO breaches (99p latency up to 820ms vs 150ms target) for a 38-minute window; non-critical endpoints saw elevated error rates. No data loss or security incident. Estimated customer-exposed requests affected: ~62k. Estimated revenue impact: low-to-medium (billing adjustments may apply).
contributing_factors: No staged canary for region-level traffic steering changes; automated failover thresholds combined with aggressive CB led to amplification.
Insufficient telemetry on per-shard KV-cache readiness at failover time; readiness gates were missing from routing decisions.
Operational runbook lacked a clear rapid rollback knob for region steering and a documented sequence for cache pre-warm.

Engineering Manager | 2026-04-07 | Update incident runbook with explicit rollback steps and a checklist for model/caching warmup during failover. (Todo)
